definition_zh: 连词；结合；同时发生
definition_en: a word that joins other words or clauses, or the act of joining two things
core_image: 两段铁轨在同一处接头，被一块夹板牢牢锁住
scene: 老师让学生把两个短句合成一句。Write two clauses, then join them with a conjunction.
sceneCN: 这里 conjunction 指「连词」（第 1 个义项：连接词或分句的虚词）；句意是先写两个分句，再用一个连词把它们连起来。

senses.title: The joining word
senses.definition: a word such as and or but that joins words or clauses
senses.definitionCN: 像 and 或 but 这样连接词或分句的虚词
senses.example: Put a conjunction between the two clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 在两个分句之间放一个连词。
senses.why: Two thoughts need a small bridge, and this word is that bridge.
senses.whyCN: 两个念头之间需要一座小桥，而这个词就是那座桥。

senses.title: A joining together
senses.definition: the state of two or more things being joined or working together
senses.definitionCN: 两件或多件事物结合、共同作用的状态
senses.example: The show is a conjunction of art and science.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览是艺术与科学的结合。
senses.why: Things that meet at one point share a moment and a meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在同一点相遇的事物，共享一个时刻与一层意义。

senses.title: A rare alignment
senses.definition: an occasion when several events or planets meet at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 若干事件或天体同时相遇的时机
senses.example: Astrologers watched the conjunction of two planets.
senses.exampleCN: 占星者观察着两颗行星的会合。
senses.why: When separate paths cross at one point, people remember the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 当几条分开的路径交于一点，人们会记住这次交会。

intro.en: Conjunction comes from Latin coniunctio, a joining, from com-, together, and iungere, to join or yoke.
intro.cn: conjunction 来自拉丁语 coniunctio，意为连接，由 com-（一起）与 iungere（连接、套上轭）构成。

items.en: Iungere meant to join or yoke animals to one bar.
items.cn: iungere 意为把牲口套在同一根横木上。

items.en: Coniunctio named a joining of things or of words.
items.cn: coniunctio 指事物的连接，也指词语的连接。

items.en: Old French conjonction kept the grammar sense alive.
items.cn: 古法语 conjonction 把这个语法含义保留下来。

items.en: English conjunction entered as the name of a joining word.
items.cn: 英语 conjunction 最初就是连接词的名字。

items.en: It now also means any coming together of events.
items.cn: 如今它也指事件的任何一次同时发生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin join base junct-, and the meaning group names other devices that hold parts together.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语连接词基 junct-，近义组列出其他把部分连在一起的东西。

entries.definition: a place where roads or railway lines meet
serving to join two things
an official order to do or stop something
a thing that joins two parts
a connection between two things
the joining of separate groups into one

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a hinge between two clauses, then move to two events meeting and to a railway joint.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个分句之间的铰链开始，再到两件事的相遇与铁轨的接头。

normal.en: Con- is together and junct- is join, so a conjunction joins two parts.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，junct- 是连接，所以连词就是把两部分接起来。

normal.en: And, but, because: three small bridges in one sentence.
normal.cn: and、but、because：一句话里的三座小桥。

normal.en: A conjunction is a hinge on which two doors of meaning swing.
normal.cn: 连词是一副铰链，两扇意义的门靠它开合。

normal.en: When two events happen at once, people call that a conjunction too.
normal.cn: 当两件事同时发生，人们也把这称作一次会合。

normal.en: Remove the word and the sentence falls into two pieces, so it was a conjunction.
normal.cn: 把这个词拿走，句子就散成两半，说明它就是连词。

abstract.en: Picture two rails locked by one steel plate.
abstract.cn: 想象两段钢轨被一块钢板锁在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hinge that lets two doors move as one.
abstract.cn: 想象一副让两扇门合为一体的铰链。

abstract.en: Picture two paths meeting under a single lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两条小路在一盏灯下汇合。

examples.en: Use a conjunction to link the two ideas.
examples.cn: 用一个连词把这两个想法连起来。

examples.en: The festival is held in conjunction with the city library.
examples.cn: 这个节庆活动是与市图书馆联合举办的。

examples.en: A strange conjunction of weather and luck saved the harvest.
examples.cn: 天气与运气的奇妙巧合保住了这一季的收成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conjunction 记成 con（一起）加 junct（连接）：把两句话一起接起来的小词，就是连词。

root: 源自拉丁语 coniunctio（com 一起 + iungere 连接），本义是连接，后专指连接词，也指事件的会合。

sensesIntro.en: From a small grammar word, to any joining of two things, and finally to events meeting at one moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个语法小词，到任何两物的结合，最后到事件在同一刻相遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge that holds two separate parts in one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副铰链把两个分开的部分连成一条线。

branches.en: The grammar sense is a single word doing the work of a hinge.
branches.cn: 语法义项就是一个词在承担铰链的工作。

branches.en: Two things joined can also work as one unit.
branches.cn: 被连接的两件事也能作为一个整体运作。

branches.en: Planets or events that meet in time form a rare conjunction.
branches.cn: 在时间上相遇的天体或事件构成罕见的会合。

branches.en: Both senses come from one image of parts held at a joint.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自同一幅画面：部分被固定在一个接头上。

branches.en: A conjunction in the sky is only a joining seen from far away.
branches.cn: 天上的会合，不过是远看时的一次连接。

intro.en: Conjunction is built on Latin com-, together, plus iungere, to join.
intro.cn: conjunction 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 iungere（连接）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin join base junct- also appears in junction, injunction and disjointed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的连接词基 junct- 也出现在 junction、injunction 与 disjointed 中。

items.meaning: a joining word or a joining
items.example: A conjunction can join two clauses.
items.exampleCN: 连词可以连接两个分句。

items.example: The conjunctive tissue holds the parts.
items.exampleCN: 连接组织把这些部分固定住。
这两个问题是连在一起的。

items.meaning: an order that binds someone to act
items.exampleCN: 法院发出了一道强制令。
我们睡在相邻的房间里。

items.meaning: not connected in a clear order
items.example: His story was disjointed and vague.
items.exampleCN: 他的叙述支离破碎又含糊。

definition_zh: 连接；联系；接通
definition_en: to join two things together, or to see how they are related
core_image: 两根电线被拧在一起，灯泡立刻亮起
scene: 电工蹲在配电箱前，把两根电线接妥。Connect the red wire to the blue one.
sceneCN: 这里 connect 指「连接」（第 1 个义项：把两物接在一起）；句意是把红线接到蓝线上。

senses.title: Join two things
senses.definition: to join two objects so that they touch or work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体接在一起，使之接触或共同运作
senses.example: Connect the printer to the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 把打印机接到电脑上。
senses.why: Two loose ends become one working line at the moment they touch.
senses.whyCN: 两个松开的端点一碰，就变成一条能工作的线。

senses.title: See a link
senses.definition: to realize that two facts or people are related
senses.definitionCN: 意识到两件事或两个人之间存在关联
senses.example: She connected the smell with her grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那股气味和祖母的厨房联系起来。
senses.why: The mind ties two memories with the same quiet thread.
senses.whyCN: 头脑用同一根安静的线，把两段记忆系在一起。

senses.title: Join a network
senses.definition: to join a phone or computer network, or to make a route open
senses.definitionCN: 接入电话或计算机网络，或使线路开通
senses.example: The call failed to connect.
senses.exampleCN: 电话没有接通。
senses.why: A network is only useful when your line reaches the others.
senses.whyCN: 网络只有在你这条线接到别人那里时才有用。

intro.en: Connect comes from Latin connectere, to bind together, from com-, together, and nectere, to tie.
intro.cn: connect 来自拉丁语 connectere，意为绑在一起，由 com-（一起）与 nectere（系、绑）构成。

items.en: Nectere meant to tie or bind one thing to another.
items.cn: nectere 意为把一物系到另一物上。

items.en: Connectere added com- to make the binding mutual.
items.cn: connectere 加上 com-，表示彼此相系。

items.en: Connexus was the participle, already tied into one.
items.cn: connexus 是它的分词形式，已经系成一体。

items.en: French connecter carried the tying sense into daily use.
items.cn: 法语 connecter 把这个系绑的含义带入日常使用。

items.en: English connect first meant to fasten two things physically.
items.cn: 英语 connect 最初指把两件东西在物理上固定在一起。

items.en: It now covers wires, ideas, people and networks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖电线、想法、人与网络。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the shape of connect, and the meaning group names other ways to hold two things together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 connect 外形相近的词，近义组列出其他把两物连在一起的说法。

entries.definition: to bring things together from different places
right and without mistakes
the older British spelling of connection

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a knot that binds two ends, then move to wires and finally to a link inside the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个把两端系住的结开始，再到电线，最后到头脑里的联想。

normal.en: Con- is together and nect- is bind, so connect is to bind two things into one.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，nect- 是绑，connect 就是把两样东西绑成一体。

normal.en: Think of a knot in a shoelace: two ends, one line.
normal.cn: 想想鞋带上的一个结：两个端头，一条线。

normal.en: A charger cable connects the wall to the phone.
normal.cn: 充电线把墙壁和手机连接起来。

normal.en: Connecting the dots means letting one fact lead to another.
normal.cn: 把线索串起来，就是让一件事引出另一件事。

normal.en: If the call does not connect, the line stays silent.
normal.cn: 电话若接不通，线路就始终沉默。

abstract.en: Picture two bare wires touching in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象两根裸露的电线在黑暗里碰在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a thread pulled tight between two beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线在两颗珠子之间被拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps lighting up at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯在同一瞬间亮起。

examples.en: Connect the cable to the socket first.
examples.cn: 先把电缆接到插座上。

examples.en: At first I did not connect the two events.
examples.cn: 起初我并没有把这两件事联系起来。

examples.en: This road connects the village with the highway.
examples.cn: 这条路把村庄和高速公路连起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 connect 记成 con（一起）加 nect（绑）：把两端绑到一起，就是连接，也指把人和事联系起来。

root: 源自拉丁语 connectere（com 一起 + nectere 系绑），本义是绑在一起，后引申为连接、联系与接通。

sensesIntro.en: From two wires tied into one line, to two memories tied in the mind, and finally to a line reaching a network.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两根电线接成一条线，到两段记忆在脑中相连，最后到线路接入网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two loose ends twisted into one working line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个松开的端头被拧成一条能工作的线。

branches.en: The first sense is the physical joining of two objects.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是两个物体在物理上的接合。

branches.en: The second sense joins ideas rather than objects.
branches.cn: 第二个义项连接的是想法而不是物体。

branches.en: The third sense opens a channel to a larger system.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是向更大的系统打开一条通道。

branches.en: A wire and a network both need a point where the line meets.
branches.cn: 电线与网络都需要一个线路相接的节点。

branches.en: Hands join objects, and the mind joins what the objects mean.
branches.cn: 手把物体接起来，头脑把物体的含义接起来。

intro.en: Connect is built on Latin com-, together, plus nectere, to bind.
intro.cn: connect 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 nectere（系绑）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bind base nect- also appears in annex and nexus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的系绑词基 nect- 也出现在 annex 与 nexus 中。

items.exampleCN: 在这里把两根管子接上。

items.meaning: a part that joins two devices

items.exampleCN: 这个镇把那片农田并了进来。

items.example: The port is a nexus of trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个港口是贸易的枢纽。

definition_zh: 连接；联系；关系；转乘衔接；人脉
definition_en: the state of being joined, a relationship, or a transport link that lets you continue a journey
core_image: 一张网把散落的点一格一格连起来
scene: 火车晚点，年轻人冲上月台时车门刚好关上。I missed the connection by two minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 connection 指「转乘衔接」（第 3 个义项：交通工具之间的接续）；句意是我差两分钟没赶上换乘。

senses.title: Being joined
senses.definition: the state of two things being joined together
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被接在一起的状态
senses.example: Check the connection between the pipe and the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下管道和水箱之间的连接。
senses.why: Two parts stop being separate once a joint holds them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了接头把两部分固定住，它们就不再彼此分开。

senses.title: A relationship
senses.definition: a relationship between people, things or ideas, including people you know
senses.definitionCN: 人、事物或想法之间的关系，也包括认识的人
senses.example: There is a clear connection between smoking and heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与心脏病之间有明显的联系。
senses.why: A link that cannot be seen still pulls two facts toward each other.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的联系，仍然会把两件事实拉在一起。

senses.title: A travel link
senses.definition: a bus, train or flight that lets you continue a journey
senses.definitionCN: 让你继续行程的接驳车、火车或航班
senses.example: The flight was late, so I missed my connection.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机晚点，所以我错过了转乘。
senses.why: One vehicle hands you to another, and the journey stays unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 一个交通工具把你交给另一个，行程因此不断。

intro.en: Connection comes from Latin connexio, a binding together, from connectere, to tie, and was spelled with an x for centuries.
intro.cn: connection 来自拉丁语 connexio，意为绑在一起，源自动词 connectere（系绑），有几个世纪都写作 x 的拼法。

items.en: Nectere meant to tie, and connectere meant to tie together.
items.cn: nectere 意为系绑，connectere 意为绑在一起。

items.en: Connexio named the joint or the act of binding.
items.cn: connexio 指接合处或绑缚的行为。

items.en: Old French connexion kept the x of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 古法语 connexion 保留了拉丁语分词里的 x。

items.en: English took the word as connexion and used it for any join.
items.cn: 英语以 connexion 的形式借入，用来指任何连接。

items.en: Writers began to spell it connection to match the Latin verb.
items.cn: 写作者开始把它拼作 connection，以贴合拉丁动词。

items.en: Connection is now standard, and it also means a train or flight link.
items.cn: 如今 connection 是标准拼法，也指火车或航班的接续。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the sound or shape of connection, and the meaning group names other kinds of link.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 connection 音形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示联系的说法。

entries.definition: the older British spelling of connection
a change that makes something right
a group of things gathered together
a relationship or a joining part
the way two people or things are connected

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two dots joined by a line, then move to people who know each other and to two trains meeting on a platform.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个被一条线连起来的点开始，再到彼此认识的人，最后到月台上相接的两趟列车。

normal.en: Con- is together, nect- is bind, and -ion makes it a thing, so a connection is a binding.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，nect- 是绑，-ion 把它变成名词，所以 connection 就是一次绑缚。

normal.en: Two dots and one line: that is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 两个点加一条线，整幅画面就是这些。

normal.en: A bad connection makes a voice break into pieces.
normal.cn: 连接不好时，说话声会碎成一片片。

normal.en: Some connections are people: a friend who knows a friend.
normal.cn: 有些 connection 指的是人：朋友的朋友。

normal.en: A missed connection leaves you standing while the train leaves.
normal.cn: 错过转乘，就只能站着看火车开走。

abstract.en: Picture two islands with one rope stretched between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两座岛之间拉着一根绳。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake that lasts a whole career.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握手支撑起整个职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a platform clock showing the same minute twice.
abstract.cn: 想象站台时钟两次指到同一分钟。

examples.en: The connection between diet and mood is well known.
examples.cn: 饮食与情绪之间的联系广为人知。

examples.en: He has good connections in the publishing world.
examples.cn: 他在出版界有很好的人脉。

examples.en: I have a connection in Paris, so the trip takes two flights.
examples.cn: 我要在巴黎转机，所以这趟行程要坐两班飞机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 connection 记成 con（一起）加 nect（绑）加 ion（名词）：绑在一起的结果，就是连接，也可以指人与人之间的门路。

root: 源自拉丁语 connexio（com 一起 + nectere 系绑），本义是绑在一起，后引申为联系、关系、人脉与交通接续。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical joint, to a relationship between facts or people, and finally to a train or flight that carries you onward.
sensesIntro.cn: 从物理上的接头，到事实或人之间的关系，最后到把你继续送走的火车或航班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two points apart, joined by one taut line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个分开的点，被一条绷紧的线连起来。

branches.en: The basic sense is a joint where two parts hold together.
branches.cn: 基本义项是两部分相互固定的接头。

branches.en: The link can be invisible yet still tie facts or people.
branches.cn: 这种联系可以看不见，却仍然把事实或人系在一起。

branches.en: In travel, the link is a vehicle that takes over from another.
branches.cn: 在旅途中，这一环是从另一班接手的交通工具。

branches.en: Both a wire and a friendship need two ends that stay in place.
branches.cn: 电线与友情都需要两端各自守在原处。

branches.en: A good contact at an airport is a personal connection and a flight link at once.
branches.cn: 机场里的熟人，同时是人脉与航班接续。

intro.en: Connection is built on Latin com-, together, plus nectere, to bind, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: connection 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 nectere（系绑）加上名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin bind base nect- also appears in nexus and annex, and its participle gave the x spelling connexio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的系绑词基 nect- 也出现在 nexus 与 annex 中，其分词形式带来了 connexio 的 x 拼法。

items.meaning: the state or act of being joined
items.exampleCN: 这个接头在压力下没有松脱。

items.exampleCN: 这些事件彼此密切相关。

items.example: The station is a nexus of the city.

definition_zh: n. 默许，纵容；共谋，暗中配合
definition_en: the act of letting wrong doing pass, often on purpose
core_image: 看守者把眼睛转向别处，钥匙却留在原地
scene: 在他的上司默许之下，走私一直没人查。The smuggling went on with the connivance of his superiors.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：connivance 指默许；句意是在上司默许下走私一直持续。

senses.title: A deliberate blind eye
senses.definition: the act of letting a wrong continue without objecting
senses.definitionCN: 不发异议地让错误持续下去
senses.example: The guard acted with the connivance of his superiors.
senses.exampleCN: 看守在上级默许下行事。
senses.why: Latin connivere means to close the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 connivere 意为闭上眼。

intro.en: Conquer comes from Latin conquirere, to seek out and obtain, from com-, fully, and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: conquer 来自拉丁语 conquirere，意为四处寻求并取得，由 com-（彻底）与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, ask or search for.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问、搜寻。

items.en: Conquirere meant to seek out thoroughly and collect.
items.cn: conquirere 意为彻底搜寻并收集。

items.en: In late Latin the word gained the military sense of winning ground.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，这个词获得了攻占土地的军事含义。

items.en: Old French conquere told of knights winning lands.
items.cn: 古法语 conquere 讲述骑士赢得土地的故事。

items.en: English conquer first meant to win by fighting.
items.cn: 英语 conquer 最初指靠打仗赢取。

items.en: It now also means to master a fear or a difficult skill.
items.cn: 如今它也指战胜恐惧或掌握一项难学的技能。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words confusingly close in sound or form, and the meaning group names other ways to win.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音或外形容易混淆的词，近义组列出其他表示赢取的说法。

senses.example: He treated the friendship as a conquest.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这段友情当成一次征服。
senses.why: The old military word is borrowed for victories of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的军事词，被借来形容心上的胜利。

intro.en: Conquest comes from Old French conqueste, from Latin conquirere, to seek out and obtain.
intro.cn: conquest 来自古法语 conqueste，源头是拉丁语 conquirere，意为四处寻求并取得。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, and conquirere meant to obtain by seeking.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求，conquirere 意为通过寻求而取得。

items.en: The noun conquestus named what had been won.
items.cn: 名词 conquestus 指已经赢到手的东西。

items.en: Old French conqueste was used for lands won in war.
items.cn: 古法语 conqueste 用于指战争中赢得的土地。

items.en: English conquest first meant the act of winning by arms.
items.cn: 英语 conquest 最初指以武力赢取的行为。

items.en: It also came to mean the thing won, not only the act.
items.cn: 它也开始指被赢得的对象，而不只是行为。

items.en: The word now extends to victories in love and in personal struggle.
items.cn: 如今这个词也扩展到爱情与个人奋斗中的胜利。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin seek base quest-, and the meaning group names other kinds of win.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语寻求词基 quest-，近义组列出其他表示胜利的词。

entries.definition: an act of politely asking for something
a long search for something important
the person who wins a conquest
success in a battle or contest
a great and celebrated victory
entries.definitionCN: 重大而值得庆祝的胜利

entries.definition: the act of taking something by force

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a map repainted, then move to the spoils that are named and to a heart won like a city.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张被改画的地图开始，再到被点名的战果，最后到像攻城一样被赢得的心。

normal.en: Conquest is conquer turned into a noun, so it is the whole event in one word.
normal.cn: conquest 是 conquer 变成名词，用一词装下整件事。

normal.en: Think of a map where one colour spreads over another.
normal.cn: 想想地图上一种颜色盖住另一种颜色。

normal.en: The act is the fighting, and the conquest is the land you can point to.
normal.cn: 行为是打仗，而 conquest 是你能用手指出的那片土地。

normal.en: A conquest needs a flag, a name and a date.
normal.cn: 一次占领需要一面旗、一个名字和一个日期。

normal.en: Love also has its conquests, though no one draws a map.
normal.cn: 爱情也有它的战果，只是没人画地图。

abstract.en: Picture a pen changing one country's colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔改变了一个国家的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a key handed over at a city gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在城门处被交出来。

abstract.en: Picture a name carved on a stone after the battle.
abstract.cn: 想象战后石头上刻下的一个名字。

examples.en: The conquest of the city took three months.
examples.cn: 攻占这座城市用了三个月。

examples.en: The old empire lived on its past conquests.
examples.cn: 这个古老帝国靠过去的战果维持。

examples.en: He saw the new friendship as a quiet conquest.
examples.cn: 他把这段新的友情看作一次安静的赢得。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conquest 记成 conquer（征服）加 st 名词尾：攻城这件事和攻下来的城池，都叫 conquest。

root: 源自拉丁语 conquirere（com 彻底 + quaerere 寻求）的名词形式，经古法语 conqueste 进入英语，指征服行为与被征服的成果。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of taking land, to the land itself, and finally to a victory won over a heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从夺取土地的行为，到土地本身，最后到在人心上取得的胜利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map repainted in one colour after an army passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：军队走过之后，地图被重新涂成一种颜色。

branches.en: The core sense is the act of seizing control.
branches.cn: 核心义项是夺取控制权这一行为。

branches.en: The result sense points at the land or people now held.
branches.cn: 结果义项指向如今被占有的土地或人民。

branches.en: The personal sense borrows the military picture for love.
branches.cn: 个人义项把军事画面借给了爱情。

branches.en: The act and its prize are two halves of one story.
branches.cn: 行为与战利品是同一个故事的两半。

branches.en: In both cases something is won and then kept.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，都是先赢得某物，再把它留住。

intro.en: Conquest carries the Latin seek base quest-, from quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: conquest 带着拉丁语的寻求词基 quest-，源自动词 quaerere（寻求）。

latinIntro.en: The same seek base appears in request, quest and question.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个寻求词基也出现在 request、quest 与 question 中。

items.meaning: the winning of land or people
a sentence that asks for an answer
items.exampleCN: 他问了一个简单的问题。
他们打听了火车的情况。

definition_zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉到的；刻意的
definition_en: awake and able to think, aware of something, or done on purpose
core_image: 病房里，病人睁开眼，第一次看清天花板
scene: 病人睁眼后先看清天花板，再认出床边的人。She was conscious of every sound in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 conscious 指「察觉到的」（第 2 个义项：意识到某事存在）；句意是她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。

pos.zh: 有意识的；清醒的；察觉的；刻意的

senses.title: Awake and aware
senses.definition: awake and able to think and feel
senses.definitionCN: 醒着，能够思考与感受
senses.example: The patient was conscious after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后病人是清醒的。
senses.why: The light is on behind the eyes again.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛后面的灯，又亮起来了。

senses.title: Noticing something
senses.definition: noticing that something exists or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事物的存在或正在发生
senses.example: She was conscious of every sound in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到房间里的每一种声音。
senses.why: Attention turns a background noise into a fact you must answer.
senses.whyCN: 注意力把背景里的声音，变成你必须回应的事实。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: deliberate and intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有意为之，而非偶然发生
senses.example: He made a conscious effort to slow down.
senses.exampleCN: 他刻意放慢了速度。
senses.why: A choice you can see yourself making is a choice you own.
senses.whyCN: 你能看见自己做出的选择，才是你真正拥有的选择。

intro.en: Conscious comes from Latin conscius, knowing with others or within oneself, from com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: conscious 来自拉丁语 conscius，意为与他人或与自己共知，由 com-（与）与 scire（知道）构成。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and conscius meant sharing that knowledge.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscius 意为共享这份知识。

items.en: A conscious person was one who knew a thing with another.
items.cn: conscius 的人，是与另一个人共同知道某事的人。

items.en: Later the knowing turned inward, meaning aware of oneself.
items.cn: 后来这种知道转向内部，表示对自身的察觉。

items.en: English conscious first meant sharing knowledge of something.
items.cn: 英语 conscious 最初指对某事知情。

items.en: It settled into the modern sense of awake and aware.
items.cn: 它逐渐固定为清醒而有察觉的现代含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscience family, and the meaning group names other words for being aware or deliberate.
note.cn: 形近组是 conscience 家族，近义组列出其他表示察觉或刻意的词。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
the state of being awake and aware
careful to do things properly
knowing that something exists
not asleep
done on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from eyes opening in a hospital bed, then move to a sound you cannot ignore and to a step you choose to take.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从病床上睁开的眼睛开始，再到无法忽略的声音，最后到你选择迈出的一步。

normal.en: Con- is with and sci- is know, so conscious is knowing with your own mind.
normal.cn: con- 是与，sci- 是知道，conscious 就是用自己的心智去知道。

normal.en: Waking up is the first conscious moment of the day.
normal.cn: 醒来，是一天中第一个有意识的时刻。

normal.en: To be conscious of a sound is to let it into your mind.
normal.cn: 察觉到一种声音，就是让它进入你的头脑。

normal.en: A conscious choice leaves a footprint you can point to.
normal.cn: 有意的选择，会留下一个你能指出的脚印。

normal.en: Half awake is not conscious enough to drive.
normal.cn: 半睡半醒，还没清醒到可以开车。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switching on above a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象床头上方一盏灯被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifted to say wait a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指举起来，示意稍等。

abstract.en: Picture a foot placed slowly and on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚缓慢而刻意地落下。

examples.en: He was conscious during the whole flight.
examples.cn: 整个飞行途中他都是清醒的。

examples.en: I am conscious of my own limits.
examples.cn: 我清楚自己的限度。

examples.en: She made a conscious choice to stay.
examples.cn: 她是有意选择留下来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conscious 记成 con（与自己一起）加 sci（知道）加 ous（形容词）：心里明白自己与周围在发生什么，就是有意识。

root: 源自拉丁语 conscius（com 与 + scire 知道），本义是共知，后转为对自身与周围有察觉，并引申出刻意的含义。

sensesIntro.en: From eyes opening, to a sound entering the mind, and finally to a step taken on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 从眼睛睁开，到声音进入头脑，最后到刻意迈出的一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp switched on behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛后面有一盏灯被点亮。

branches.en: The first sense is simply being awake and able to think.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是醒着并能思考。

branches.en: The second sense points outward at something noticed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项目光向外，指向被注意到的事物。

branches.en: The third sense turns awareness into a chosen act.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把觉察变成有意的行动。

branches.en: You must be awake before anything can be noticed.
branches.cn: 必须先醒着，才可能注意到什么。

branches.en: Noticing a habit is the first step to changing it on purpose.
branches.cn: 察觉一个习惯，是刻意改变它的第一步。

intro.en: Conscious is built on Latin com-, with, plus scire, to know, and the adjective ending -ous.
intro.cn: conscious 由拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）加上形容词词尾 -ous 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in science, conscience and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 science、conscience 与 omniscient 中。

items.exampleCN: 药物让他的意识变得迟钝。

items.example: He was unconscious on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他倒在地板上失去了知觉。

items.example: A subconscious habit shaped her choice.
items.exampleCN: 一个潜意识习惯塑造了她的选择。

items.meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong

items.exampleCN: 没有哪位老师无所不知。

definition_zh: 意识；知觉；觉悟
definition_en: the state of being awake and able to think, or awareness of a shared issue
core_image: 麻醉退去，天花板的灯光一点点变清晰
scene: 麻醉慢慢退去，病人终于认出病房里的窗帘。He lost consciousness for a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 consciousness 指「知觉」（第 2 个义项：清醒并感知外界的状态）；句意是他有几秒钟失去了知觉。

senses.title: Being awake
senses.definition: the state of being awake and able to think and feel
senses.definitionCN: 醒着并能思考、感受的状态
senses.example: He slowly regained consciousness in the ambulance.
senses.exampleCN: 他在救护车里慢慢恢复了知觉。
senses.why: The inner light goes out, and then it comes back.
senses.whyCN: 心里的灯先熄灭，然后又亮起来。

senses.title: Awareness of something
senses.definition: the fact of noticing or caring about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题的注意与关心
senses.example: There is growing consciousness of water waste.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对水资源浪费的意识正在增强。
senses.why: A problem becomes real to a person only when it is noticed.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题被人注意到，才对这个人变得真实。

senses.title: A shared mindset
senses.definition: the shared beliefs and feelings of a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体共有的信念与感受
senses.example: The movement changed public consciousness.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动改变了公众意识。
senses.why: Many private minds can settle into one common weather.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人的心思，可以沉淀成一种共同的天气。

intro.en: Consciousness is conscious plus the noun ending -ness, built on Latin conscius, knowing with oneself.
intro.cn: consciousness 是 conscious 加名词词尾 -ness，源头是拉丁语 conscius，意为与自己共知。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and conscius meant sharing knowledge.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscius 意为共享知识。

items.en: The noun conscientia named inward knowledge of oneself.
items.cn: 名词 conscientia 指对自身的内部知识。

items.en: English formed consciousness from conscious and -ness.
items.cn: 英语用 conscious 加 -ness 造出 consciousness。

items.en: Psychology made it the name of the waking mind.
items.cn: 心理学把它定为清醒心智的名称。

items.en: It now also means a group's shared awareness of an issue.
items.cn: 如今它也指一个群体对某个问题的共同意识。

note.en: The look-alike group is the conscience family, and the meaning group names other states of noticing.
note.cn: 形近组是 conscience 家族，近义组列出其他表示察觉状态的词。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong
awake and aware
careful to do what is right
knowledge that something exists
the state of being quick to notice
the part of a person that thinks and feels

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a waking patient, then move to a problem people begin to see and to a mood shared by a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从醒来的病人开始，再到人们开始看见的问题，最后到人群共有的情绪。

normal.en: Conscious plus -ness is simply the state of being conscious.
normal.cn: conscious 加 -ness，就是处于有意识状态。

normal.en: Losing consciousness is a light going out; regaining it is the switch clicking back.
normal.cn: 失去知觉是灯灭了，恢复知觉是开关又咔哒一声。

normal.en: Social consciousness begins when a private worry becomes a public word.
normal.cn: 社会意识始于私人的担忧变成一个公开的词。

normal.en: A raised consciousness is a raised hand.
normal.cn: 被唤醒的觉悟，就是一只举起来的手。

normal.en: The word sounds like conscience but points at the light, not the judge.
normal.cn: 这个词听起来像 conscience，但它指那盏灯，而不是法官。

abstract.en: Picture a white ceiling slowly coming into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象白色的天花板慢慢变清晰。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd all turning to look at one sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人同时转头看同一块牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held up in a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗大厅里举起的一只手。

examples.en: The blow did not cost him consciousness.
examples.cn: 那一击没有让他失去知觉。

examples.en: Environmental consciousness has grown in the past decade.
examples.cn: 环保意识在过去十年里增强了。

examples.en: She spoke with a new consciousness of her own rights.
examples.cn: 她带着对自身权利的新觉悟说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consciousness 记成 conscious（有意识的）加 ness（状态）：灯亮着的那种状态，就是意识。

root: 由拉丁语 conscius（com 与 + scire 知道）经 conscious 加 -ness 构成，指清醒感知的状态，后扩展为群体觉悟。

sensesIntro.en: From the light of a waking mind, to noticing a problem, and finally to a belief shared by many.
sensesIntro.cn: 从清醒心智的光，到注意到某个问题，最后到许多人共有的信念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light that can go out and come back on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏会熄灭也会重新亮起的灯。

branches.en: The first sense is the bare state of being awake.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是醒着这一基本状态。

branches.en: The second sense adds an object: something is noticed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项加上了对象：某件事被注意到。

branches.en: The third sense spreads that noticing across a whole group.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这种注意扩展到整个群体。

branches.en: Being awake is the ground on which any noticing stands.
branches.cn: 醒着，是任何察觉得以成立的地面。

branches.en: One person's noticing becomes a group's consciousness when others agree.
branches.cn: 一个人的察觉，在别人认同后就成了群体的意识。

intro.en: Consciousness is conscious plus -ness, from Latin com-, with, and scire, to know.
intro.cn: consciousness 是 conscious 加 -ness，源自拉丁语 com-（与）与 scire（知道）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin know base sci- also appears in science, conscience and omniscient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的知道词基 sci- 也出现在 science、conscience 与 omniscient 中。

items.exampleCN: 他在黎明时恢复了知觉。

items.example: She was conscious of the risk.
He consciously kept his voice low.
The image stayed in her subconscious.
items.exampleCN: 那个画面留在她的潜意识里。

items.meaning: the inner sense of right and wrong

items.exampleCN: 那个声音听起来无所不知。

definition_zh: 连续的；接连的；连贯的；结果性的
definition_en: following one after another without an interruption, or following as a result
core_image: 日历上六页接连翻过，每一页的日期都紧挨着前一页，中间没有空白的一页
scene: 跑道上电子计时牌一站一站翻过，同一名选手的名字连续出现，中间没有空缺。She won the title for three consecutive seasons.
sceneCN: 这里指一段时间内一次接一次、中间没有断开（第 1 个义项：时间上接连无间断）；句意为她连续三个赛季夺得冠军。图中可辨识物件：电子计时牌、选手名次、连成一列的赛季记录。

pos.zh: 连续的；接连的；连贯的；结果性的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「连续地；接连地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「连续性」
由同一拉丁词干构成的名词，义为「连续；顺序」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不连续的」

senses.title: Following in time without a break
senses.definition: happening in one period after another with nothing missing in between
senses.definitionCN: 一个时段接一个时段地发生，中间没有缺失
senses.example: The team trained for five consecutive days before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，这支队伍连续训练了五天。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow closely, so the word begins with one thing pressing right behind another.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为紧跟，因此这个词最初就是一物紧贴另一物之后。

senses.title: Counting in an unbroken run
senses.definition: used of numbers or amounts that follow in an unbroken order
senses.definitionCN: 用于按不间断次序相随的数字或数量
senses.example: Write the consecutive numbers from one to ten.
senses.exampleCN: 写出一到十的连续数字。
senses.why: Counting is the plainest example of following on, with no value skipped between two terms.
senses.whyCN: 计数是「依次相随」最朴素的例子，两个数之间没有跳过的值。

senses.title: A run of wins
senses.definition: describing victories or successes that come one after another without a defeat between them
senses.definitionCN: 指一场接一场的胜利或成功，中间没有失败
senses.example: The club recorded four consecutive victories in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部在联赛中取得四连胜。
senses.why: Sport counts streaks, and a streak is exactly a series with no gap in it.
senses.whyCN: 体育要数连续纪录，而连续纪录正是一个没有缺口的序列。

senses.title: Adjacent in a series
senses.definition: placed next to each other in an ordered set, as with numbers or seats
senses.definitionCN: 在有序集合中彼此相邻，如号码或座位
senses.example: The tickets bear consecutive serial numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些票的编号是连号的。
senses.why: When items are numbered, following on means occupying the very next place.
senses.whyCN: 当物件被编号时，依次相随便意味着占据紧接着的那一位。

senses.title: A chain of linked events
senses.definition: describing events in which each one follows from the one before it
senses.definitionCN: 指每个事件都由前一个事件引出的情形
senses.example: The report describes a consecutive chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一连串前后相承的失误。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to result from, so following in time can become following as a consequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词也意为「由……导致」，因此时间上的相随可以变成因果上的相承。

senses.title: The grammar of result
senses.definition: naming a clause that expresses the result of what the main clause states
senses.definitionCN: 指表达主句所述内容之结果的从句
senses.example: The grammar book explains how a consecutive clause expresses result.
senses.exampleCN: 这本语法书讲解结果从句如何表达结果。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the adjective for clauses where the second statement follows from the first.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借这个形容词指第二个陈述由第一个陈述引出的从句。

senses.title: Unbroken shifts or operation
senses.definition: describing work periods that run one after another without a pause
senses.definitionCN: 指一个接一个运行、中间不停顿的工作时段
senses.example: The plant runs three consecutive shifts during the peak season.
senses.exampleCN: 生产旺季，工厂连续开三个班次。
senses.why: Industry measures time in shifts, and consecutive shifts leave no idle gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 工业以班次计量时间，而连续班次之间没有空闲的间隔。

senses.title: Year-after-year climate records
senses.definition: used of weather or climate data gathered over an unbroken series of years
senses.definitionCN: 用于在连续多年中收集的天气或气候数据
senses.example: Records show three consecutive dry years in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 记录显示该地区连续三年干旱。
senses.why: Climate science compares year to year, and a run of years with no break is the basic unit of a trend.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学逐年比较，而一段没有中断的年份正是趋势的基本单位。

intro.en: Consecutive comes from Latin consequi, to follow closely, from con-, together, and sequi, to follow; the past participle consecutus produced Late Latin consecutivus, which English borrowed in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「consequi」紧跟、随后，由「con-」一起与「sequi」跟随构成；过去分词「consecutus」产生晚期拉丁语「consecutivus」，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: To follow is the core of the word, and the same verb stands behind sequence and sequel.
items.cn: 跟随是这个词的核心，同一个动词也构成「sequence」与「sequel」的词源。

items.en: The prefix means together or along with, so following becomes following on.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为一起或随之，于是「跟随」变成「紧跟着」。

items.en: The verb meant to follow closely, to come after, and also to result from something.
items.cn: 这个动词意为紧跟、随后，也意为由某事物导致。

items.en: The past participle described what has followed, and it is the stem before the English ending.
items.cn: 这个过去分词描述已经跟随而来的事物，是英语词尾之前的词干。

items.en: The later adjective named things that follow in order or form a series.
items.cn: 这个晚期形容词指按次序相随或构成序列的事物。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century for things coming one after another.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个形容词，用于一个接一个到来的事物。

note.en: The first group looks like consecutive or shares its Latin stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of things following in order. Note that successive stresses the order of items, from Latin sub- and cedere, to come after, while consecutive stresses that no gap separates them.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「consecutive」相近或共享拉丁词干；第二组是与「依次跟随」相邻的说法。要注意「successive」强调各项的次序，出自拉丁语「sub-」与「cedere」跟随在后；而「consecutive」强调中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: In an unbroken order, one after another.
The state of following in sequence, a rare noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随的状态，是同一词干的罕见名词。

entries.definition: The quality of being unbroken in sequence.
A result that follows from an action; it shares the Latin verb but not the sense of sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指由行为引出的结果；共享拉丁动词，但没有「连续」之义。

entries.definition: To set something apart as sacred; it looks close but belongs to a word for making sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物定为神圣；形近但属于「使神圣」那一系。

entries.definition: Following in order, one after another, with emphasis on the sequence rather than on gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随，强调次序，而不强调有无间隔。

entries.definition: Arranged in a fixed order, one step or item after another.
entries.definitionCN: 指按固定次序排列，一步或一项接一项。

entries.definition: Going on without any stop or break, often of time or movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指不停顿、不中断，常用于时间或运动。

entries.definition: Not broken off at any point, used of a stretch of time or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段时间或活动在任何节点都未被打断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin follow verb behind the word, its real family and the everyday things counted in runs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁语「跟随」动词、真实同族词，以及日常中成串计数的事物。

normal.en: The Latin sequi is to follow, and con- adds the sense of coming right along after.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「sequi」是跟随，「con-」加上「紧随其后」的意思。

normal.en: Consecutive days, consecutive years and consecutive wins all count things with no gap.
normal.cn: 连续几天、连续数年与连胜，数的都是没有缺口的事物。

normal.en: Consecutive numbers are neighbours on the number line, like adjacent seats in a row.
normal.cn: 连号数字是数轴上的邻居，就像一排里相邻的座位。

normal.en: A consecutive clause is named for the result that follows from the main statement.
normal.cn: 结果从句得名于由主句陈述引出的结果。

normal.en: Consecutive interpreting follows speech in chunks, one stretch after another.
normal.cn: 交替传译跟着讲话分段进行，一段接一段。

abstract.en: A gap is the only enemy of this word: if one day is missing, the run is broken.
abstract.cn: 缺口是这个词唯一的敌人：只要缺了一天，连续就断了。

abstract.en: Time is not a line but a stack of pages, and consecutive means no page was torn out.
abstract.cn: 时间不是一条线，而是一叠纸页，连续就意味着没有一页被撕掉。

abstract.en: A streak is fragile because it is counted backwards; one loss erases the whole series.
abstract.cn: 连续纪录之所以脆弱，是因为它被倒着数；一场失利就抹掉整串。

examples.en: The region suffered three consecutive summers of drought.
examples.cn: 该地区连续三个夏天遭遇干旱。

examples.en: Her consecutive victories surprised the whole circuit.
examples.cn: 她的连胜让整个巡回赛都感到意外。

examples.en: Number the pages in consecutive order from front to back.
examples.cn: 把书页从前往后按连续顺序编号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯塞丘提夫」——一个接一个，中间不空档：连续的、接连的

root: 拉丁语「consequi」意为紧跟、随后，由「con-」一起加「sequi」跟随构成，过去分词「consecutus」，晚期拉丁语「consecutivus」；英语十七世纪引入。它与「secare」切无关，因此与「section」「sector」不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from time to counting to sport: unbroken time, counting, a run of wins, adjacent items, a chain of causes, the result clause, unbroken shifts, and year-by-year climate records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从时间走到计数再走到体育：不间断的时间、连续计数、连胜、相邻项、因果链、结果从句、连续班次，以及逐年气候记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: calendar pages turn in a stack, each date touching the next with no blank page between.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历一叠页接连翻过，每个日期都紧贴下一个，中间没有空白页。

branches.en: THE UNBROKEN STRETCH: time or a count runs on with nothing missing.
branches.cn: 不间断的一段：时间或计数一路延续，什么都不缺。

branches.en: THE RUN AND THE SERIES: wins stack up, and neighbouring items share an edge.
branches.cn: 连续纪录与序列：胜利层层累积，相邻各项共用一条边。

branches.en: THE CHAIN OF CAUSES: one event follows another as its outcome.
branches.cn: 因果链：一个事件作为结果跟随另一个事件。

branches.en: THE GRAMMATICAL RESULT: a clause states what follows from the main clause.
branches.cn: 语法上的结果：从句陈述由主句引出的内容。

branches.en: THE WORKING AND CLIMATE RECORD: unbroken shifts, and statistics over year after year.
branches.cn: 作业与气候记录：连续的班次，以及逐年累积的统计。

intro.en: Consecutive is a Latin adjective of following, and its endings and prefixes keep the sense of a series with no break.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示跟随的拉丁形容词，它的词尾与前缀都保留着「序列不断」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sequi, to follow, and consequi, to follow closely; the adjective consecutivus comes from the past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「sequi」跟随与「consequi」紧跟；形容词「consecutivus」来自其过去分词。

items.example: The verb is the root of sequence and sequel as well.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也是「sequence」与「sequel」的词根。

items.example: The prefix makes following into following on.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」变成「紧跟着」。

items.structure: Latin verb from con- and sequi
items.example: The verb joins the two halves of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把这一意思的两半合在一起。

items.example: The participle supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了形容词的词干。

items.example: The form passed through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式经法语进入英语。

items.example: It marks the English adjective consecutive.

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from con- and sequi

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「连续地」
由同一拉丁词干构成的名词，义为「连续；顺序」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「连续性」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不连续的」

definition_zh: 共识；共同意见；一致意见
definition_en: general agreement among a group, especially after discussion, or the view most people in a field hold
core_image: 一圈人围桌而坐，最后所有手都放在同一张纸上
scene: 表决之前，主持人再问一遍，无人再提出新的修改。After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
sceneCN: 这里 consensus 指「一群人在讨论之后形成的共同意见」（第 1 个义项：群体内的一致）；句意为辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。可辨识物件：长桌、摊开的报告、举手表决前的沉默、记录本。

senses.title: Agreement across a group
senses.titleCN: 一个群体内部的共同意见
senses.definition: a general agreement reached by the members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一群成员形成的普遍一致
senses.example: After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。
senses.why: Latin consensus simply meant 'agreement', and English kept that breadth: the noun names the state without saying how it was reached.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 consensus 本来就只表示「一致」，英语保留了这个宽度：这个名词命名状态，不说明它是怎么达成的。

senses.title: The view most people hold
senses.definition: the opinion that prevails in a field or a population at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或人群在某一时期占上风的看法
senses.example: The consensus in the field is that the warming is real.
senses.exampleCN: 该领域的主流看法是变暖确实在发生。
senses.why: when a shared view becomes the background assumption, consensus means the default position rather than a fresh agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当共同看法变成背景假设，consensus 指的就是默认立场，而不是新达成的协议。

senses.title: Agreement produced by talk
senses.titleCN: 经讨论而非表决形成的一致
senses.definition: a shared position arrived at through discussion rather than through a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨论而非正式表决得到的共同立场
senses.example: Consensus was reached without a formal ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 没有正式投票就形成了共识。
senses.why: meetings needed a word for agreement that is felt in the room before it is counted, and this noun supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 会议需要一个词，来形容那种先在会场里被感觉到、之后才被计数的同意，这个名词正好补上。

senses.title: Agreement among experts
senses.definition: the settled judgement of specialists in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域专门研究者已定下来的判断
senses.example: Scientific consensus on the age of the rock took decades to form.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这块岩石年龄的科学共识，花了几十年才形成。
senses.why: science does not vote, but it does converge, and the noun describes that convergence without implying unanimity.
senses.whyCN: 科学不作表决，却会收敛；这个名词描述这种收敛，但并不暗示全体一致。

senses.title: Sympathy among body parts
senses.titleCN: 旧医学：身体各部分的同感
senses.definition: an old physiological notion that the organs act in sympathy with one another
senses.definitionCN: 旧生理学中的观念：各器官彼此同感相应
senses.example: Early physicians wrote of a consensus among the organs.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医生写到各器官之间的同感。
senses.why: the Latin noun was borrowed first for bodily sympathy, because parts that act together were said to feel together.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最早被借用来指身体各部的同感，因为共同起作用的部位被说成「一同感受」。

senses.title: Cross-party agreement
senses.definition: a shared position adopted by rival political groups
senses.definitionCN: 对立政治团体共同采取的立场
senses.example: A consensus emerged between the parties on health funding.
senses.exampleCN: 各党在医疗拨款上出现了共同立场。
senses.why: politics uses the word precisely when rivals stop contesting an issue, which is agreement seen as a truce.
senses.whyCN: 政界在对手停止争夺某议题时才用这个词，那是把一致看作停战。

senses.title: A process short of unanimity
senses.titleCN: 不要求全体赞成的一致程序
senses.definition: a decision method in which no one blocks a proposal, though not everyone need approve it
senses.definitionCN: 一种决定方式：无人阻止提议，尽管并非人人都赞成
senses.example: Consensus decision-making does not mean everyone must agree.
senses.exampleCN: 共识决策并不等于人人都必须赞成。
senses.why: groups that cannot afford majority rule redefine consensus as the absence of objection, and the noun follows them.
senses.whyCN: 无法承受多数决的团体，把共识重新定义为「无人反对」，这个名词也跟着这样用。

senses.title: The averaged professional forecast
senses.titleCN: 市场或预测中的平均预期
senses.definition: the central estimate that analysts or forecasters collectively expect
senses.definitionCN: 分析师或预测者集体预期的中心估计
senses.example: The consensus forecast puts growth at two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 市场平均预期把增长定在百分之二。
senses.why: finance takes the many separate views and treats their middle as one voice, which is consensus by aggregation.
senses.whyCN: 金融界把许多分散的看法取其中间，当作一个声音，这是靠汇总得到的共识。

intro.en: Consensus is a Latin noun built on consentire 'to feel together', from com- 'together' and sentire 'to feel'. English borrowed it in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consensus 是一个拉丁名词，出自 consentire「一同感受」，由 com-「共同」与 sentire「感受」构成。英语在十七世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think', and it also gives English sense, sentiment and sentence through related Latin forms.
items.cn: sentire 意为「感觉、知觉、思考」，它还经相关的拉丁形式衍生出英语的 sense、sentiment 与 sentence。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire produced consentire, 'to feel together, to be of one mind, to agree'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire 构成 consentire，意为「一同感受、心意相同、同意」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun consensus named the state of feeling together: agreement, accord, harmony.
items.cn: 第四变格法名词 consensus 命名「一同感受」的状态：一致、和谐、同心。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century, first in learned writing about the body and about philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最初见于关于身体与哲学的学术写作。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries it meant general agreement in any group, and later produced the political phrase consensus politics.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，它指任何群体中的普遍一致，后来又产生「共识政治」这一说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest English example is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the deeper pre-Latin shape of sentire is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对最早的英语书证年代说法不一；sentire 在拉丁语之前的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like consensus but belong to other Latin families; group two holds nouns for collective agreement, each with a different width.
note.cn: 第一组收形似 consensus、却属于别的拉丁词族的词；第二组收表示集体一致的名词，覆盖面各不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin censere 'to assess, estimate', the verb behind censorship and censor: a counting of the population, not a state of agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 censere「评估、估算」，也是 censorship 与 censor 背后的动词：指人口清点，而非意见一致。

entries.definition: Built on the same consentire, but it names permission given by one party rather than agreement across a group.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 consentire，但它指一方给出的许可，而非一群人的普遍一致。

entries.definition: The adjective of this noun: resting on mutual consent, used of contracts, relations and shared reality.
entries.definitionCN: 本名词的形容词：以双方同意为基础，用于合同、关系与共同认定的现实。

entries.definition: A compound naming the work of bringing a group to a shared position before a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词构成的复合词，指在决定之前把一群人带到共同立场的工作。

entries.definition: Complete agreement of all members; consensus can exist without every member approving.
entries.definitionCN: 全体成员完全一致；而 consensus 可以在并非人人赞成时存在。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between parties, often states; it is an instrument, where consensus is a state of mind.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式协定，常指国家间；它是一份文书，而 consensus 是一种心态。

entries.definition: The part of a question on which opponents already agree; it need not cover the whole issue.
entries.definitionCN: 争论各方已经同意的那一部分；它不必覆盖整个议题。

entries.definition: The opinion held by more than half; it is a matter of numbers, whereas consensus is a matter of acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过半数持有的意见；它靠数人头，而 consensus 靠接受程度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire 'feel': to feel together, hence to agree.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire「感受」：一同感受，因而同意。

normal.en: The family runs consensus, consensual, consent, consenting, consensus-building.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 consensus、consensual、consent、consenting、consensus-building。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the scale: broad consensus, scientific consensus, the consensus view.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出规模：广泛共识、科学共识、主流看法。

normal.en: The plural is consensuses, since the Latin fourth-declension ending does not survive in English.
normal.cn: 复数是 consensuses，因为拉丁第四变格法的词尾在英语中没有保留。

normal.en: The near relative census comes from a different verb and means a count, not an agreement.
normal.cn: 形近的 census 出自另一个动词，意为清点，而非一致。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs in which every person finally leans the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，最后每个人都朝同一个方向倾身。

abstract.en: Picture many small streams joining into one wide, slow river.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小溪汇成一条宽而缓的河。

abstract.en: Picture a room going quiet not because anyone was silenced but because no one wished to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子安静下来，不是有人被制止，而是无人再想开口。

examples.en: No consensus emerged, so the chair postponed the vote.
examples.cn: 没有形成共识，于是主席推迟了表决。

examples.en: The consensus among clinicians is to wait another week.
examples.cn: 临床医生之间的共识是再等一周。

examples.en: Consensus in a large group often hides two or three determined minorities.
examples.cn: 大团体里的共识，常常掩盖着两三个坚定的少数派。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ sensus（感觉）」——大家感觉一样 → 共识

root: 拉丁 consensus「一致」出自 consentire「一同感受」= com-（共同）+ sentire（感受）；英语十七世纪借入，最初用于生理与哲学论述。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a room reaching agreement to a market averaging forecasts: the same noun covers a feeling shared by bodies, by committees, by experts and by traders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一间屋子里达成一致，一直到市场把预测取平均：同一个名词涵盖身体、委员会、专家与交易者所共享的那种「同感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people at one table, every hand finally resting on the same sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈人围着一张桌子，最后所有手都落在同一张纸上。

branches.en: THE ROOM: agreement in a group, produced by talk rather than by a count.
branches.cn: 会场：群体中的一致，由谈话而非计数产生。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the prevailing view, and the settled judgement of specialists.
branches.cn: 领域：占上风的看法，以及专家已定下的判断。

branches.en: THE BODY: the oldest loan sense, where organs are said to feel together.

definition_zh: 后果；结果；重要性

senses.title: A result

senses.title: Importance

senses.title: A logical conclusion

senses.exampleCN: 由这些事实可以得出一个无法回避的结论。
senses.why: Reason walks forward, and this is the place it must stop.

items.en: Consequentia named what follows from something else.

definition_zh: 保护；保存；节约
definition_en: the protection of nature and old things, or the careful use of resources
core_image: 护林员把幼苗周围的杂草轻轻拨开
scene: 护林员在幼苗周围插上木牌，请游人绕行。The conservation of the old forest took thirty years.

senses.title: Protecting nature
senses.definition: the protection of animals, plants and natural places
senses.definitionCN: 对动植物与自然环境的保护
senses.example: The conservation of the old forest took thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片古老森林的保护工作持续了三十年。
senses.why: A living place survives only if someone guards it on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一片有生命的土地，只有被有意守护才能存续。

senses.title: Careful use
senses.definition: the careful use of resources so that they are not wasted
senses.definitionCN: 对资源的节约使用，避免浪费
senses.example: Water conservation begins at home.
senses.exampleCN: 节约用水从家里开始。
senses.why: What is used slowly lasts longer than what is spent fast.
senses.whyCN: 慢慢用的东西，比快速耗掉的东西用得久。

senses.title: Keeping in good condition
senses.definition: the work of keeping old buildings or objects in good condition
senses.definitionCN: 使旧建筑或旧物保持良好状态的工作
senses.example: The conservation of the wall took months.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙的修复用了好几个月。
senses.why: Old things do not stay old by accident; someone stops the decay.
senses.whyCN: 旧东西不会自己保持原样，总有人拦住了腐朽。

intro.cn: conservation 来自拉丁语 conservatio，意为共同守护，由 com-（一起）与 servare（保全）构成。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe or to watch over.
items.cn: servare 意为保全或看守。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of conservation, and the meaning group names other kinds of keeping safe.

normal.cn: 旧墙能保持旧貌，只因为有人花钱修它。

examples.en: Energy conservation saves money as well as fuel.

examples.en: The museum is famous for the conservation of old paper.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆以修复旧纸张闻名。

branches.en: Nature and energy both need the same habit of not wasting.

definition_zh: 保守的；守旧的；谨慎的；保守派；偏低的
definition_en: preferring old ways and slow change, cautious, or a deliberately low estimate
core_image: 老人试了新沙发，还是坐回那张旧木椅
scene: 搬家后老人试了试新沙发，又坐回旧木椅。He gave a conservative estimate of the cost.
sceneCN: 这里 conservative 指「偏低的；谨慎的」（第 3 个义项：估计故意低于真实数字）；句意是他对费用给出了一个偏低的估计。

senses.title: Preferring the old
senses.definition: preferring traditional ways and slow change
senses.definitionCN: 偏好传统方式与缓慢的改变
senses.example: His family is conservative about clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他家人对穿着比较保守。
senses.why: What has lasted feels safer than what is only new.
senses.whyCN: 已经延续下来的东西，比只是新鲜的东西更让人安心。

senses.title: Cautious
senses.definition: careful and not willing to take risks
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎而不愿承担风险
senses.example: The bank took a conservative view of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 银行对市场持谨慎看法。
senses.why: A low guess is a cushion against being wrong.
senses.whyCN: 把话说低一点，是给判断失误留的垫子。

senses.title: A low estimate

senses.exampleCN: 他对费用给出了一个偏低的估计。
senses.why: Promise little, and the final number can only surprise upward.
senses.whyCN: 把话说小，最后的数字只可能向上给人惊喜。

items.en: Glass plant rooms took the same name.
items.cn: 十九世纪玻璃花房沿用此名。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the conserv- stem; the near-meaning group names schools and glasshouses.
note.cn: 形近组共享 conserv- 词干；近义组列出学校与温室。

entries.definition: Protection of valued things.
A person who repairs treasures.
Favouring tradition.
A school of special study.
An institution of higher study.
A glass building for plants.
A house of glass for plants.

normalIntro.en: A conservatory preserves music in one sense and plants in another.
normalIntro.cn: conservatory 一义保存音乐，一义保存植物。

normal.en: Conservare means to keep safe.
normal.cn: conservare 意为保全。

normal.en: A conservatory keeps what is precious inside.
normal.cn: 温室或学院把珍贵之物留在里面。

normal.en: Music conservatories keep a tradition alive.
normal.cn: 音乐学院让传统延续。

normal.en: Glass conservatories keep plants warm.
normal.cn: 玻璃温室为植物保暖。

normal.en: The ending -ory marks a place.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 表示场所。

abstract.en: A glass roof full of green light.
abstract.cn: 充满绿光的玻璃屋顶。

abstract.en: A practice room with one piano.
abstract.cn: 只有一架钢琴的练习室。

abstract.en: A warm room in a cold month.
abstract.cn: 寒冷月份里的暖房。

examples.en: He won a place at the national conservatory.
examples.cn: 他考入了国家音乐学院。

examples.en: The conservatory is full of ferns.
examples.cn: 温室里满是蕨类植物。

examples.en: Conservatories train many orchestral players.
examples.cn: 音乐学院培养许多乐团演奏者。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（完全）+ serv（保存）+ -atory（场所）→ 保存之所，后指音乐学院与温室。

root: 拉丁 conservare（保全）→ 意大利语 conservatorio（收容所）→ 英语 conservatory

sensesIntro.en: A kept place, whether for music or for growing things.
sensesIntro.cn: 一处被守护的地方，或保存音乐，或培育植物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: green light under a glass roof
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃屋顶下的绿光

branches.en: A piano heard through a door.
branches.cn: 门后传来的钢琴声。

branches.en: A hall of practising students.
branches.cn: 满是练习学生的厅堂。

branches.en: Ferns behind tall glass.
branches.cn: 高玻璃后的蕨类。

branches.en: Tomatoes ripening in winter.
branches.cn: 冬天里成熟的番茄。

branches.en: A house that keeps things growing.
branches.cn: 让事物继续生长的地方。

intro.en: Conservatory ends in the place suffix -ory.
intro.cn: conservatory 以表场所的词尾 -ory 结尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin conservare is to keep safe; conservatorium names a place of keeping.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 conservare 意为保全，conservatorium 指保存之所。
